text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who has been told by doctors to limit his workload, arrived in the Kremlin on Tuesday and is likely to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, the president's office said.
Yeltsin, 65, has been recovering from pneumonia in a government guest house outside Moscow.

Aides said he unexpectedly visited the Kremlin last week, his first trip there since he was taken ill with pneumonia on January 6. The president has not appeared on television since then, raising suspicions about the severity of his condition.
After Yeltsin's quintuple heart surgery on November 5, his office was quicker to release footage of the president than they have been for his latest ailment, pneumonia in both lungs.
Yeltsin on Monday cancelled a planned trip to the Netherlands on the recommendation of his doctors, who had advised him not to fly while he is recovering from pneumonia.
But aides said French President Jacques Chirac would go ahead with a Moscow visit this Sunday.

Doctors say the pneumonia is not linked to Yeltsin's heart problems or the operation he underwent last November. But they have warned him not to hurry back to work despite his apparent eagerness to resume duties in the face of opposition demands that he step down.
